planItem: 77.44.7.A — Invalid Inspector content.href must block draft Save and separate Publish
finding: The Inspector lifecycle browser test showed javascript: URL feedback and then corrected it, but did not attempt Save or Publish while the shared validation error was active. The high-risk guard therefore lacked a direct browser assertion.
testChange: tests/browser/editor-inspector-lifecycle.test.js now makes a valid unsaved button-label edit first so Publish is enabled, enters javascript:alert(1) in content.href, and attempts both Save and Publish. It asserts that neither API request is posted, the server draft and public snapshot remain unchanged, the unsafe text remains available for correction, and the normal corrected href lifecycle still passes.

browser.environment: Local Chromium with the test's loopback HTTP fixture; the default sandbox denied loopback with EPERM, so the unchanged test was run with local network permission.

iterations: The first default-sandbox attempt was blocked because loopback listen returned EPERM.

The first permitted browser run found that Publish was disabled because the fixture had no valid unsaved change; the fixture was updated to create a valid pending label edit before attempting invalid-href Publish.

A subsequent locator attempt targeted the shared authored-content component, but button text is intentionally rendered by the specialized plain-text editor; the test now uses that existing node-scoped control.
